title: Distinct Subsequences
keyIdea: dp[j] = number of ways t[0..j) appears as a subsequence of the part of s read so far. For each letter of s, for j from n down to 1: if s[i − 1] == t[j − 1], dp[j] += dp[j − 1]. dp[0] = 1.

approaches.name: One-row DP
approaches.idea: I wrote this one (you didn't paste code). dp[0] = 1; for each letter of s, for j = n..1: if it matches t[j − 1], dp[j] += dp[j − 1]. Unsigned so middle values may wrap safely.
approaches.why: Every (letter of s, letter of t) pair once; one row.

quiz.q: Why loop j from right to left?
options: So dp[j − 1] is still the old value and a single letter of s isn't used twice
Left to right is the same
1: the empty t appears exactly once in any prefix of s

quiz.q: On a match, why add and not set?
options: Ways that skip this letter of s still count; ways that use it are added

steps: Count distinct index choices, not distinct strings?
Brute force: try all subsequences of s. Cost?
